title: Rigidity of Ricci-Pinched Complete Self-Shrinkers in Arbitrary Codimension
summary: Let $M$ be an $n$-dimensional complete connected self-shrinker in $\mathbb{R}^{n+p}$. Denote by $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $\mathbf{H}$ the Ricci curvature tensor and the mean curvature vector of $M$, respectively. We prove that if the self-shrinker $M$ satisfies $\operatorname{Ric}\ge(\frac{n-2}{n^2}+\varepsilon_n)|\mathbf{H}|^2g$, then $M$ is either a linear subspace or a round shrinking sphere, where $\varepsilon_n$ is an explicit positive constant equal to $\frac{1}{3n^2}+O\left(\frac{1}{n^5}\right)$.
